nodes.title: Approaches to Interpretation of Theater and Performance: Global Perspective
nodes.description: Seminar, four hours. Introduction to basic methods of interpretation in theater and performance throughout world. Topics illustrated by faculty members and guest speakers, visits to off-campus theaters, and reading from contemporary plays. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Performance
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; studio, four hours. Investigation of phenomenon of performance and role of performer in theatrical events, including interpretation of drama through performance. Examination of various forms of theatrical performance and styles of expression, and development of acting, voice, and movement skills. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Play Reading and Analysis
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours. Provides base for subsequent study in theater. Development of techniques of play reading and habits of scholarship useful to further study in each of theater’s subdisciplines, including acting, directing, design, playwriting, and critical study. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Design
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; studio, six hours. Exploration of visual interpretation of drama. Study of styles and techniques of design, collaborative role of designer, principles of design for scenery, lighting, costumes, and sound. Both technical and aesthetic groundwork for further study. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Design
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; studio, six hours. Exploration of visual interpretation of drama. Study of styles and techniques of design, collaborative role of designer, principles of design for scenery, lighting, costumes, and sound. Both technical and aesthetic groundwork for further study. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Design
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; studio, six hours. Exploration of visual interpretation of drama. Study of styles and techniques of design, collaborative role of designer, principles of design for scenery, lighting, costumes, and sound. Both technical and aesthetic groundwork for further study. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Directing
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; studio, four hours. Investigation of role of director in theatrical production and theories of play direction, with emphasis on analysis and interpretation of dramatic work and its realization in production. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Musical Literacy for Singing Actors
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Reading and translating musical notation in treble clef; defining common musical terminologies; basic rhythm-reading and diatonic sight-singing in all major keys. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Musical Literacy for Singing Actors
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. More advanced sight-singing, incorporating minor keys, chromatic scales, internal key changes, and bass clef; exploration of song form, musical theater score formats, and harmonic/contrapuntal singing. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Acting Foundations: Voice
nodes.description: (Formerly numbered 24A.) Studio/lecture/discussion, six hours. Study of basic vocal technique for actor, with emphasis on resonance, range, and power. Physiological foundations for subsequent training and theoretical foundations to enlarge the actor’s sense of a vocal practice. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Acting Foundations: Movement
nodes.description: Studio/lecture/discussion, six hours. Broad investigation of movement in performance, with emphasis on ensemble performance and the actor’s craft. Physiological foundations for subsequent training and theoretical foundations to enlarge the actor’s sense of a physical practice. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Group Singing Techniques
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Introduction to singing techniques, with emphasis on bel canto training. Exploration of how singing voice works and how to achieve optimal vocal sound and musicality while preserving vocal health. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Group Singing Techniques
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Advanced singing techniques, focusing on strategies for producing consistently dynamic, efficient, and musical vocal sound, and how to build stamina and range while preserving vocal health. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production
nodes.description: Laboratory, three to six hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including stage management or member of production crew. Combination of courses 50A, 50B, 50C, and 50D may not be taken for more than 8 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production
nodes.description: Laboratory, six to nine hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including stage management or member of production crew. Combination of courses 50A, 50B, 50C, and 50D may not be taken for more than 8 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production
nodes.description: Laboratory, nine to twelve hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including stage management or member of production crew. Combination of courses 50A, 50B, 50C, and 50D may not be taken for more than 8 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production
nodes.description: Laboratory, twelve to sixteen hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including stage management or member of production crew. Combination of courses 50A, 50B, 50C, and 50D may not be taken for more than 8 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Global Histories of Theater and Performance I
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to histories of theater and performance from across world, with emphasis on ancient world through 18th century. Introduction to global aesthetic theories and historiographical research methods. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Global Histories of Theater and Performance II
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to histories and historiographies of theater and performance from across world, with emphasis from 18th century through 21st century. Introduction to representational modalities from melodrama to performance art and theoretical approaches from Marxism to poststructuralism. Letter grading.

nodes.title: The Actor's Imagination I
nodes.description: Studio/lecture/discussion, six hours. Cultivation of dramatic imagination and clarity of intention. Letter grading.

nodes.title: The Actor’s Imagination II
nodes.description: Studio/lecture/discussion, six hours. Continued cultivation of dramatic imagination and clarity of intention, with increased emphasis on relationship, partnering, and scene work. Letter grading.

nodes.title: The Actor’s Toolbox I
nodes.description: Studio, six hours. Study of the actor as storyteller. Students gain understanding of the arc of a role and learn to work independently. Letter grading.

nodes.title: The Actor’s Toolbox II
nodes.description: Studio, six hours. Continuation of course 116A, including an introduction to heightened language and/or post-realist texts. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Teaching Artist Fundamentals
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Introduction to teaching artist techniques and the creation of storytelling projects through K-12 engaged pedagogy. Exploration of approaches to the interrelationships of arts to traditional learning disciplines by the facilitation of creative activities and lesson plan construction. Letter grading.

nodes.title: ArtsBridge Teaching Practicum
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Teaching artist residency in K-12 Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) classrooms. Weekly meetings to develop teaching materials that integrate the performing arts into standard curriculum. The LAUSD placement culminates in a final creative project presented by the host classroom. May be repeated once for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Vocal Power and Clarity I
nodes.description: Studio, three to four hours. Cultivation of personal vocal practice, voicing dramatic and nondramatic texts. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Vocal Power and Clarity II
nodes.description: Studio, three to four hours. Continued cultivation of personal vocal practice, voicing dramatic and nondramatic texts, with greater focus on contemporary dramatic texts. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Vocal Dexterity I
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Vocal and rhetorical challenges presented by heightened dramatic texts. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Intermediate Playwriting: Full-Length Play Part I
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Introduction to process of conceiving, researching, and developing full-length plays. Students begin drafting full-length plays. May be repeated twice for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Playwriting: Full-Length Play Capstone
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Same as course 131B, but taken for capstone credit. Completion of writing of full-length plays begun in course 131A, with rehearsed readings of student capstone plays. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Singing: Individual Instruction
nodes.description: Studio, one hour. Designed to advance proper vocal technique, focusing on breath support, vowel shape, range expression, and overall mastery of vocal instrument. May be repeated four times for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production and Performance
nodes.description: Laboratory, three to six hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including performance in project or production, stage management, assistant director, dramaturg, member of crew, or assignment as designer or assistant on production. May be repeated 15 times for credit. Combination of courses 150A, 150B, 150C, and 150D may not be taken for more than 16 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production and Performance
nodes.description: Laboratory, six to nine hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including performance in project or production, stage management, assistant director, dramaturg, member of crew, or assignment as designer or assistant on production. May be repeated seven times for credit. Combination of courses 150A, 150B, 150C, and 150D may not be taken for more than 16 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production and Performance
nodes.description: Laboratory, nine to 12 hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including performance in project or production, stage management, assistant director, dramaturg, member of crew, or assignment as designer or assistant on production. May be repeated four times for credit. Combination of courses 150A, 150B, 150C, and 150D may not be taken for more than 16 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Theater Production and Performance
nodes.description: Laboratory, 12 to 16 hours. Laboratory experience in various aspects of theater production, including performance in project or production, stage management, assistant director, dramaturg, member of crew, or assignment as designer or assistant on production. May be repeated three times for credit. Combination of courses 150A, 150B, 150C, and 150D may not be taken for more than 16 units. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Directing for Stage
nodes.description: Lecture/studio, four hours. Culminating development of directorial methods, with particular emphasis on challenges of style in text and production. Students direct scenes under laboratory conditions in alternative stage configurations. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Career Preparation for Integrated Studies
nodes.description: Lecture, four to six hours. Focus on preparing for working professionally in theatre and performance after graduation for students in the integrated studies emphasis. Students learn about job searching and internships, creating resumes, interviews, creating a web site, pitching and presenting their own work, options for secondary higher education, etc. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Career Preparation for Actor
nodes.description: Lecture/studio, four to six hours. Limited to seniors. Preparation for professional career as actor in film, television, theater, and commercials. Topics include audition preparation, head shots, résumés, agents, managers, casting directors, producers, unions, survival skills, professional development. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Audition Preparation for Singing Actor
nodes.description: Lecture/studio, three hours. Preparation for a professional career as a musical theater performer in theater, film, television, and other audio/visual venues. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Design Assignment: Assistant Designer
nodes.description: Studio, six hours. Laboratory experience as assistant designer, including participation in preparation and realization of scenic, lighting, costume, or sound designs. May be repeated twice. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Production Design Assignment: Designer
nodes.description: Studio, six hours. Laboratory experience as designer, including preparation and realization of scenic, lighting, costume, or sound designs. May be repeated twice. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Stage Managing Techniques
nodes.description: Studio, six hours. Professional duties of stage manager. Problems of unions, professional auditions, organization, scheduling, out-of-town openings, Broadway openings, and responsibilities of lengthy run. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Project in Stage Management
nodes.description: Studio, nine hours. Laboratory experience in professional duties of assistant stage manager, including participation as assistant stage manager in preproduction, rehearsal, and performance phases of productions. May be repeated once for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Project in Stage Management
nodes.description: Studio, 12 hours. Laboratory experience in professional duties of stage manager, including participation as stage manager in preproduction, rehearsal, and performance phases of productions. Problems of unions, auditions, organization, scheduling, and responsibilities of lengthy run. May be repeated three times for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Senior Project
nodes.description: Lecture or studio, three hours. Preparation of conceptual or creative project to provide culminating experience in production of creative or research work. May be repeated twice for credit. Letter grading.
